summary: The dominant cause of INC-006 was a sudden reset/emptying of the shared platform-owned redis-cache at 13:22Z, which triggered a cold-cache rebuild storm and blocked pricing-engine's synchronous calls to market-data-service past deadline. Confidence in H1 is medium (0.58, capped by the Critic): redis-cache's hit_ratio_pct collapsed 95.33%→11.55% and memory_pct 70.54%→6.38% in the same 13:22Z bucket while evictions_per_min stayed flat (~2.3-3.7/min), proving a content reset rather than memory-pressure eviction (F19, F20, F21). The failure shape is a single-minute step with slow cold re-warm at constant load (~641.9 req/s, 647.09 in the onset bucket) (F7, F8, F13), and the observed pricing-engine symptoms — p99 step to 2227ms, 5xx to 3.21%, and "deadline exceeded: market-data-service took 827-8456ms" errors — are those of a blocked consumer, not the faulting component (F9, F10). H2 (fault inside market-data-service) remains a residual alternative because its own cpu/memory/restart metrics could not be retrieved, and the user-facing blast radius upstream of pricing-engine was not measured; both are scope details of a proven origin and do not change the fix that applies.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared redis-cache emptied/reset at 13:22Z (external flush/failover/restart) → cold-cache rebuild storm → pricing-engine deadline-exceeded
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 13:22:00Z the platform-owned shared redis-cache lost its contents in a step change: hit_ratio_pct collapsed from ~95-96% to 11.55% and memory_pct collapsed from ~70.5% to 6.38% in the same minute bucket, then both climbed back slowly as the cache was re-populated from cold — and evictions_per_min stayed flat (~3 keys/min) throughout, so this was NOT maxmemory-driven eviction but an external reset/restart/failover/flush. With quote keys gone, market-data-service entered a 'cache miss storm', rebuilding each quote from the exchange feed snapshot (1034-8748ms), which blocked pricing-engine's synchronous HTTP calls past deadline (827-8456ms), stepping pricing-engine p99 from ~60ms to 2227ms and 5xx from ~0.2% to ~3.2-4.3% at the same 13:22Z minute, with both metric series decaying slowly as the cache re-warmed. No trigger change is enumerable: the only deployment in the whole window (auth-service dep-5604, 11:30Z) is off the pricing-engine graph and 1h52m early, and there were zero config/flag changes, so the origin is an unrecorded infrastructure event on the cache (HIST-107 analogue).

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache contents are dropped in a step at 13:22Z: hit_ratio 95-96% → 11.55%, memory 70.5% → 6.38%, evictions flat (~3/min), then slow re-warm (memory 6.38% → 29.94% by 14:58)
Because evictions did not spike, the emptying is not maxmemory pressure — it is a reset/flush/restart/failover of the shared cache (mechanism inferred; redis-cache exposes no restart/uptime metric)
With quote keys absent, market-data-service logs 289 'cache miss storm: quote:<id> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot' WARNs from 13:22:25Z, rebuild times 1034-8748ms

ranked_hypotheses.title: Fault inside market-data-service: its own snapshot-rebuild path became slow, so pricing-engine calls time out
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The origin is market-data-service, not the cache. Its quote snapshot/rebuild path degraded at 13:22Z — e.g. its exchange-gateway calls slowed, its own thread/connection pool saturated, or a pathological input made rebuilds 1-8.7s — which both lengthened its responses to pricing-engine and produced the 'cache miss storm' WARNs (each rebuild taking 1034-8748ms, i.e. too slow to fill the cache within budget). redis-cache need not be faulty: if market-data-service simply could not populate or serve in time, the shared cache's hit ratio would look degraded from the perspective of misses. What weakens this hypothesis is that redis-cache's absolute memory_pct collapsed from ~70% to 6.38% and its hit ratio collapsed to 11.55% in a single minute bucket, which a slow rebuild path alone does not explain; and no market-data-service restart/saturation metric could be retrieved (tc-011 unavailable, cpu/memory/restart queries hit budget_exhausted).

Rebuilds of quote:<id> take 1034-8748ms, emitted as 'cache miss storm: quote:<id> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot'
market-data-service's own p99 steps 39.8ms → 1916.65ms and error_rate 0.18% → 3.23% at 13:22Z
pricing-engine's outbound calls to market-data-service block 827-8456ms, yielding 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms'
pricing-engine p99 and 5xx step at 13:22Z and decay slowly

assumptions: redis-cache's hit_ratio/memory collapse is explainable by market-data-service failing to populate it, rather than by a cache-side reset
market-data-service itself had no slow/restarting state — its cpu/memory/restart metrics were never retrieved
exchange-gateway or market-data-service's own pool degraded with no enumerable change (no deployment touched either in the window)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load-driven capacity saturation / cold-cache storm from traffic, with no triggering change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: No change is responsible: genuine quote traffic exceeded what the shared quote read path could serve, or a cold cache plus a request surge triggered mass rebuilds that saturated the read path. pricing-engine's own CPU/memory stayed flat, so any saturation would have to sit on market-data-service or redis-cache. This is now strongly contradicted: pricing-engine's request_rate was measured flat (~640 req/s, 621-658 pre-onset, 647.09 in the onset bucket, 625-680 after) with no step or ramp at 13:22Z, so the latency/error step occurred at constant incoming load — removing the load-surge mechanism. The failure shape (single-minute step, then slow recovery) is also characteristic of a discrete event, not gradual capacity exhaustion.

market-data-service's rebuild capacity is exceeded, producing the cache-miss storm with 1034-8748ms rebuilds

recommended_actions.action: Treat the shared redis-cache reset as the incident origin: confirm with the platform/Redis owners whether a failover, restart, manual FLUSH, or infrastructure event (e.g., node failover, upgrade, or scheduled maintenance) hit the shared redis-cache at 2026-04-09T13:22Z, and capture the failover/restart timestamp from the Redis control plane (not available in the metric set).
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 attributes the whole chain to an external reset of the shared cache (F19, F20, F21) with no enumerable trigger (F1, F3). Confirming the cache-side event closes the single unverified origin hop of the leading hypothesis and isolates whether a change-system gap allowed it.

recommended_actions.action: If the cache reset is confirmed as a Redis-side restart/failover, restore warm cache state deliberately: pre-warm the shared redis-cache from market-data-service's snapshot path before shifting full quote traffic back, or enable gradual cache warming to avoid a second cold-start amplification under production load.
recommended_actions.rationale: The observed failure is a cold-cache rebuild storm with slow recovery (F11, F19, F20); controlled pre-warming removes the rebuild-storm mechanism that blocked pricing-engine calls past deadline (F9).

recommended_actions.action: Add or enable a shared-redis-cache health signal — restart/uptime, latency/response-time, and connected_clients — and alert on a simultaneous hit_ratio + memory step (the exact F19/F20 signature) so a silent content reset pages immediately instead of surfacing as pricing-engine latency.
recommended_actions.rationale: redis-cache exposes no restart/uptime/latency metric (only connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct), so the reset was only inferable after the fact from simultaneous hit_ratio and memory collapse (F19, F20, F21).

recommended_actions.action: Verify the user-facing blast radius by measuring api-gateway and order-service latency_p99 for 12:30-14:59Z, which was never retrieved; confirm whether the reported 2-3s quote load time reproduces at the API layer.

recommended_actions.action: Close the H1-vs-H2 residual by retrieving market-data-service cpu_pct, memory_pct, request_rate, and restarts for 12:30-14:59Z (previously budget_exhausted) and correlating the 1034-8748ms rebuild times against redis-cache wait vs exchange-gateway wait.

recommended_actions.action: Eliminate the change-system blind spot: ensure platform-owned infrastructure components (shared redis-cache) have auditable events (failover, restart, flush, maintenance) recorded in the same change/event store as service deployments, since the 13:22Z reset has no enumerable trigger despite complete deployment (F1, F2) and config (F3) enumeration.

recommended_actions.action: Harden pricing-engine against dependency stalls: add a bounded cache-miss/rebuild budget or circuit-breaker on the market-data-service call path, and consider serving last-known-good quotes under deadline pressure, so a downstream cold-cache rebuild cannot drive p99 to 2+ seconds and 4% 5xx.
recommended_actions.rationale: pricing-engine's own CPU/memory were flat (F10); the failure was purely a blocked synchronous call 'market-data-service took 827-8456ms' (F9), so resilience belongs at the call boundary.

data_gaps: redis-cache exposes no restart-count, uptime, or latency/response-time metric (available: connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct), and its connected_clients/cpu_pct values were not retrieved — so no direct restart/failover/promotion event for the cache is confirmed; the reset is inferred from the simultaneous hit_ratio + memory collapse (F19, F20, F21).

api-gateway and order-service latency_p99_ms were not retrieved (only error_rate), so downstream latency propagation to the user-facing API layer (the reported 2-3s quote load) is inferred only from pricing-engine p99, not measured.

Outbound call latency from market-data-service to exchange-gateway vs to redis-cache (wait-time correlation of the 1034-8748ms rebuilds) was not retrievable, so it cannot be determined whether the slow rebuilds correlate with cache wait time or exchange-gateway wait time.

api-gateway latency/error metric query and the broader INFO-level '401' log search were not completed (budget_exhausted / timeout), so auth 401/403 absence is confirmed at WARN only, not across all log levels.

pricing-engine thread/connection-pool and GC metrics do not exist in the available metric list, and deployment enumeration was completed only by splitting into two partial-free windows after a partial first query and a timed-out retry, so a deployment in a shard that failed only during the unsplit query cannot be fully excluded.

what_would_change_the_conclusion: Retrieving market-data-service cpu_pct/memory_pct/restarts showing its own independent restart or resource saturation beginning at 13:22Z would elevate H2 (fault inside market-data-service) over H1, since the cache miss storm could then be a symptom of market-data-service failing to serve rather than the cache being reset.

Evidence that redis-cache's hit_ratio/memory collapse is an artifact of the miss storm rather than a genuine content reset (e.g., a Redis restart/uptime metric showing no reset, or a counter that explains the memory drop without a flush) would break the core premise of H1.

Discovery of a recorded change or config/flag update on redis-cache or market-data-service near 13:22Z (within the unverified Apr 8 config slice or a shard that failed during the unsplit deployments query) would reinterpret the origin as a bad/triggered change rather than an unrecorded infrastructure event.
Measurement showing pricing-engine request_rate or a downstream queue actually ramped at 13:22Z (contradicting the flat ~641.9 req/s) would revive the load-driven capacity mechanism of H4.

Evidence that the 1034-8748ms rebuilds correlate with exchange-gateway wait time rather than cache wait time would shift the origin downstream of the cache, favoring a dependency/exchange-gateway fault path.
